title: Lead Scoring

metaDescription: Everything on lead scoring for Indian B2B teams: how Fit × Intent × Quality grading works, how to set it up, and the concepts, guides and tools that make it work.
dek: Lead scoring decides which lead your rep calls next — and getting it right is the difference between a busy team and a closing team. This is the complete map of how Leadkaun grades every lead A–F in real time, the concepts behind it, and the guides to set it up.

quickAnswer.question: What is lead scoring and how does it work?
quickAnswer.answer: Lead scoring ranks each lead by how likely it is to convert. Leadkaun grades every lead A–F in under 500ms across three independent scores — Fit (ICP match), Intent (live engagement, which decays as leads go silent), and Quality (data reliability) — with transparent weights, so reps work the highest-probability leads first.

keyTakeaways: Three independent scores — Fit, Intent, Quality — combine into one A–F grade.
Intent decays automatically when a lead goes quiet, so stale Grade A leads fall on their own.
Transparent weights beat a black-box AI score — reps trust a grade they can see.
A graded lead is in the queue within the first hour of setup.

faqs.q: Is lead scoring worth it for a small team?
faqs.a: Yes — a small team feels a wrong call-order most acutely, because every rep-hour counts. Automatic A–F grading means the first calls of the day go to the leads most likely to close, not the newest ones.

faqs.q: How is this different from my CRM's lead scoring?
faqs.a: Most CRM scoring is a single opaque points number. Leadkaun uses three transparent scores with weights you can audit, and intent that decays automatically — no manager intervention to keep grades honest.

faqs.q: How is this different from activity tracking?
faqs.a: Activity tracking counts outputs — calls, emails, messages. Behaviour tracking measures the decisions inside that activity: was the Grade A lead called in time, did the follow-up happen on schedule, was the right lead worked next. Behaviour predicts revenue; activity just proves busyness.

The opposite. Because logging is three taps, the data is complete on its own — so managers coach on a few specific, measurable signals instead of hovering. You point at a slow Grade A response, not a person's effort.
